items.text: Why the oil does the work
How to make cannabis infused honey

runs: Cannabis infused honey doesn't need a long flower infusion. If you've made canna-coconut oil, whisking it into warm honey takes about 20 minutes and turns one master infusion into a sweetener for tea, toast and sauces.

body.text: Why the oil does the work

runs: THC barely dissolves in water, and honey is mostly sugar and water, so flower steeped in it gives up far less THC than it would to fat. Fat dissolves THC readily. That's why this starts with canna-coconut oil, made with the jar method in our

Spread the oil's THC over the finished honey. Suppose your oil tops out around 13 mg per teaspoon: 2 tablespoons hold about 78 mg. Whisked into 1/2 cup of honey, that makes about 10 tablespoons, so roughly 8 mg per tablespoon or 2.6 mg per teaspoon. A drizzle is hard to judge, so measure it with a spoon, keep the first serving to a teaspoon or less and let at least 2 hours go by. See our
Thick, raw honey holds oil droplets better than runny honey. Add melted canna-coconut oil and, if you like, a pinch of sunflower lecithin, an emulsifier that helps the two stay blended.

body.text: How to make cannabis infused honey

runs: Warm the honey jar in a pan of hot water until it's runny, not hot, and melt the oil the same way. Pour the oil into the honey in a thin stream, whisking the whole time, and keep at it for a few minutes as the blend cools. If oil separates later, warm the jar and stir before measuring.

Honey keeps well, but homemade infused oil doesn't: the CDC advises refrigerating homemade herb oils and using them within 4 days. Give the blend the same care, freezing any extra in small portions. Write the mg per teaspoon, the date and the word "infused" on every side of the jar, and store it apart from your everyday honey, up where kids and pets can't reach.

1/2 cup thick raw honey
2 tablespoons canna-coconut oil, melted
Optional: 1/8 teaspoon sunflower lecithin
Set the honey, in a heatproof jar or bowl, in a pan of hot (not boiling) water until it loosens, about 5 minutes.
Melt the canna-coconut oil the same way and measure 2 tablespoons.
Drizzle the oil into the honey in a thin stream, whisking steadily. Add the lecithin, if using.
Keep whisking for 3 to 5 minutes as the mixture cools so the oil stays blended.
Pour into a clean jar, write the strength per teaspoon and today's date on it, and refrigerate. Use within 4 days or freeze small portions.

Estimate only: oil at about 13 mg per teaspoon gives 2 tablespoons roughly 78 mg. Spread through 10 tablespoons (30 teaspoons) of honey, that's about 8 mg per tablespoon, or 2.6 mg per teaspoon. That's a ceiling: your oil's actual strength hinges on the flower behind it and on what the decarb and infusion lost along the way. A teaspoon or less is plenty to start; give it at least 2 hours before any more. Mark the jar and park it beyond the reach of kids and pets.

items.q: Why use coconut oil instead of infusing honey with flower?

runs: Because THC dissolves in fat, not in sugar or water. Steeping flower in honey extracts far less and leaves plant bits behind, while an oil infusion has already done that work. Coconut oil tastes mild, blends into warm honey easily and firms up in the fridge.

items.q: Will the oil separate from the honey?

runs: It can, especially with runny honey or in a warm kitchen. Thick honey, steady whisking as it cools and a pinch of lecithin all help. If you see a layer of oil, warm the jar gently and stir before measuring, since the THC sits in the oil.

items.q: How much canna-honey is one serving?

runs: Work it out from your batch, not the spoon. In the example above, a teaspoon carries about 2.6 mg at most. That sits close to the 2.5 mg ceiling Canadian public-health officials recommend for a first edible, so a level teaspoon or a little less is a sensible start.
